name: security-mongodb-role-boundaries-review
intent: MongoDB database/collection actions and delegated role authority
artifacts: Authentication database, user roles/inheritance, resource patterns and requested collection or administrative operation.
trace: Resolve the actual principal and action/resource grant, including whether a wrapper supplies privileged credentials for caller-selected namespaces.
experiment: Use a local database with two owned namespaces and synthetic documents; compare permitted action and one forbidden collection/role operation.
disproof: Connection success or database-name discovery is not document-read or administrative authority.
repair: Limit effective roles and wrapper namespace selection, testing legitimate queries and restricted resources.
branch_decisions: Evaluate inherited roles with database and collection resource scope, including anyResource or cluster actions. Authentication database is not necessarily the database being accessed. A driver connection succeeding proves login only; record the exact collection operation allowed to the restricted principal and do not infer write, admin or cross-database rights from a read.
operational_method: Identify self-hosted versus Atlas role definitions and the effective deployment API before interpreting familiar role names. Expand inherited privileges into action/resource pairs and inspect role-grant/user-administration authority separately from collection reads. Use supplied users/roles definitions and one owned collection operation; a permitted role-administration action can create a distinct delegation path, but do not grant a production role to demonstrate it.
